parts.label: whole
parts.display_text: A 24 g object executes simple harmonic motion with total energy 2.2 × 10⁻⁴ J. In one complete oscillation it travels 14 mm. Calculate its angular frequency.

answer.text: A full oscillation covers 4A, so A = 3.5 × 10⁻³ m. E = ½mω²A² gives ω = √[2E/(mA²)] = 39 rad s⁻¹.

fep-4702f1ae6785e44e-q10:whole.hint: Use the amplitude to fix the total energy, then compare the position with equilibrium.
notes: For SHM, v² = ω²(A² − x²), and total energy is ½mω²A². The kinetic energy depends on how far the oscillator is from equilibrium.
At a turning point speed is zero; at equilibrium its magnitude is ωA. Doubling amplitude changes total energy by a factor of four, not two.
